title: signal-weighted-regression-deep-dive-2026-06-26
summary: Biweekly deep-dive that reweights signals from different eval pipelines to produce a prioritized remediation queue for newly onboarded models and promptsets. Emphasis on high-impact failures that correlate with production SLA regressions.
content:
Context:
This note synthesizes the last two weeks of onboarding eval signals (automated evals, human labels, production telemetry) and applies a simple signal-weighting heuristic to surface clusters of failures that likely explain customer-observed quality drops.

Why different: current weekly digests show raw counts across promptsets; this doc attempts to combine severity, spread, and signal confidence into a single prioritization score for action routing. Useful for sprint planning and for handing to solutions engineering.

Signal sources we used (pipeline IDs):
- eval/auto/onboard_v3 (synthetic tasks)
- eval/human/onboard_random_sample (3% sample, rubric A)
- prod/telemetry/regression-alerts (customer incidents)
- analysis/prompt-compat/formatting-checker (structure-sensitive checks)

Signal-weighting heuristic (TL;DR):
PriorityScore = 0.5*ProdImpact + 0.3*HumanSeverity + 0.2*AutoSignalConfidence
Where:
- ProdImpact (0-1): normalized count of production incidents attributable to the model or route
- HumanSeverity (0-1): mean severity from human labels (major/minor/ok mapped to 1/0.5/0)
- AutoSignalConfidence (0-1): model of how many auto checks triggered and how deterministic they are (e.g., hallucination detector, structure checker)
Rationale: production incidents matter most; we keep human labels high but not dominant because coverage is small.

Snapshot metrics (two-week window 2026-06-12 -> 2026-06-25):
- Total onboarding promptsets evaluated: 118
- New model variants onboarded: 7
- Prod incidents correlated with onboarding models: 18 (↑45% vs previous window)
- Human-labeled failures flagged: 92 samples (26% severe)
- Auto-eval flags: 410 triggers across checks

Top failure clusters after weighting (ordered):
1) Prefix-loss / context-truncation cluster
   - PriorityScore: 0.82
   - Observations: Lossy prefix caching + new model KV alignment causes truncation on long instructions for promptset "enterprise-summarize-v2".
   - Signal mix: prod incidents (7), human severe (12), auto-format (34)
   - Proposed short-term fix: reduce prefix cache TTL for affected route and enable sequence-preserving fallback.
   - Owner: Marcus Chen (serving-runtime)
   - Linked issue: RD-PR-1123

2) Table-format hallucination spike
   - PriorityScore: 0.69
   - Observations: Model fabricates numeric rows when asked to normalize CSV -> seen across two promptsets used by data connectors.
   - Signal mix: prod incidents (4), human severe (8), auto-hallucination-detector (56)
   - Proposed fix: tighten post-processing filter on numeric rows and add reranker that prefers source-consistent rows.
   - Owner: Sofia Martinez (applied-ml)

3) Stylistic regression on system-instructed tone (safety-adjacent)
   - PriorityScore: 0.61
   - Observations: New model variant drifts toward abrupt/short replies for high-certainty prompts, affecting UX in customer chat flows.
   - Signal mix: prod incidents (3), human moderate (6), auto-style (12)
   - Proposed fix: rebaseline system prompt, adjust temperature, add style-loss term in light-finetune.
   - Owner: Liam O'Connor (solutions-eng)

4) Tokenization mismatch for emoji-heavy inputs
   - PriorityScore: 0.45
   - Observations: Discrepancy between tokenizer used in offline evals vs runtime tokenizer causing off-by-one generation errors in small fraction of samples.
   - Owner: Platform infra (TBD)

Evidence table (plain text):
Cluster | prod_inc | human_sev_pct | auto_triggers | priority
Prefix-loss | 7 | 0.4 | 34 | 0.82
Table-halluc | 4 | 0.28 | 56 | 0.69
Tone-drift | 3 | 0.21 | 12 | 0.61
Tok-mismatch | 1 | 0.05 | 6 | 0.45

Triaging rules applied: (to make decisions fast)
- Any cluster with PriorityScore >= 0.7 -> hot lane (immediate patch + rollback plan)
- 0.5 <= Score < 0.7 -> warm lane (investigate + short-term mitigations)
- Score < 0.5 -> monitor and defer to next cycle unless production incidents spike

Concrete action plan for sprint (2-week):
- Hot lane:
  * Prefix-loss: Marcus to land cache-ttl experiment (RD-PR-1123) by 2026-06-28, deploy to canary; monitor prefix-truncation rate and customer error rate.
  * Table-halluc: Sofia to ship post-filter rules and reranker stub by 2026-07-01; A/B against current route.
- Warm lane:
  * Tone-drift: run temp/system-prompt grid (3x) and human-eval 300-sample batch. Owner: Liam.
  * Tokenizer: platform to validate tokenizer binary hashes used during build vs runtime images; quick fix if mismatch found.

Monitoring queries to add (examples):
- eval.query:count(where=prefix_truncated AND model in onboarded_variants, window=24h)
- telemetry.metric:halluc_row_rate(route=data-connectors*, window=1h)
- human.review:severity_hist(promptset=enterprise-summarize-v2, last=500)

Acceptance criteria for closure of hot-lane tickets:
- Prefix-truncation rate reduced by >= 80% on canary traffic with no latency degradation > 5%
- Table-halluc A/B shows halluc_row_rate drop >= 60% without degrading recall on numeric extraction tasks

Risks & rollback plan:
- Cache-ttl change could increase memory pressure; rollback procedure: revert cache config, rehydrate KV caches, and route traffic to fallback variant.
- Reranker deployment may increase P50 latency; mitigation: limit reranker to <10% sampling first, then ramp.

Notes / open questions:
- Is the tokenizer mismatch stemming from image build differences or from an older tokenizer wheel used by data-connectors? (Action: Platform to produce a file-hash diff by 2026-06-27)
- Do we want to promote the hallucinatory-row detector from auto-flag -> runtime block for some enterprise routes? Need legal/privacy check.

Meeting invite template for hot-lane sync (use calendar link):
- Title: Hot-lane regression sync: Prefix-loss + Table-halluc
- Cadence: daily 09:30 for next 5 days (15 mins)
- Desired attendees: Marcus, Sofia, Liam, product-rep, solutions-eng

Next steps / owner confirmations:
- Marcus: confirm canary config by 2026-06-28 (comment in RD-PR-1123)
- Sofia: upload reranker notes + eval plan to Confluence and link into PR by 2026-06-29
- Liam: assemble human-eval batch and recruit 6 reviewers by 2026-06-30

If anything urgent pops up ping #applied-ml-regressions on Slack and add the linear ticket to the top of the hot-lane triage board.

Appendix: quick reproducibility checklist (for on-call):
1) Pull failing promptset: onboarding/enterprise-summarize-v2 from eval bucket
2) Run local inference with model variant X (hash: abc123) and compare tokens with runtime image
3) Run hallucination-detector on output and check auto flag thresholds
4) If production incident exists, attach telemetry window and customer id to linear ticket

End of note.
